where: Exam traps, trap 5 (also Section 2 bullet 'Below the feed use the stripping line')
problem: The rule 'use the rectifying line while x > x_F and the stripping line while x < x_F' is true only for a saturated liquid feed, where the q-line is vertical at x_F. For any other feed (two-phase, saturated vapour, subcooled liquid) the changeover point is the x-coordinate of P, the intersection of the two operating lines, which is not x_F. For a two-phase feed x_P is greater than x_F, so a student following this rule switches too early and gets a wrong stage count.
fix: Switch operating lines when the step crosses the q-line: keep the rectifying line until the horizontal step takes x below x_P (the x of point P), then use the stripping line. Only when q = 1 does x_P equal x_F.

problem: 'q is the fraction of feed that is liquid' is only true for feeds between bubble point and dew point. A subcooled liquid feed has q > 1 and a superheated vapour feed has q < 0, where 'fraction liquid' has no meaning; these two cases are also missing from the bullet list.
fix: Define q as the heat needed to turn 1 mol of feed into saturated vapour divided by the molar latent heat (equivalently the moles of liquid formed per mole of feed for feeds between bubble and dew point). Add: q > 1, subcooled liquid, slope q/(q−1) positive and greater than 1; q < 0, superheated vapour, slope positive but small.

problem: 'Draw the q-line at x_F' tells the reader the q-line is always the vertical x = x_F. It is vertical only for a saturated liquid feed.
fix: Say: draw the q-line through (x_F, x_F) with slope q/(q−1); for a saturated liquid feed this is the vertical line x = x_F.

problem: x* appears in 'This gives x* at the current y' without being defined, and the equilibrium formula above defines only y*.
fix: Define it where it first appears: x* is the liquid mole fraction in equilibrium with the vapour of composition y, obtained from y* = αx/(1 + (α−1)x) solved for x.

problem: 'Count each horizontal-vertical pair as one theoretical stage' is inaccurate at the bottom: the last step is often a horizontal move only, with no vertical move after it, yet it still counts as a stage.
fix: Say: each horizontal step to the equilibrium curve is one equilibrium contact; the vertical move only sets up the next step, and the final step may be horizontal alone.

problem: 'Real trays are more than theoretical stages' is garbled; it reads as if trays are a larger quantity than stages rather than a larger number of trays being needed.
fix: The number of real trays needed is greater than the theoretical stage count, because tray efficiency is below one.

problem: 'The feed enters at liquid composition x_F' is misleading: x_F is the overall feed composition and the q-line passes through (x_F, x_F) for vapour and two-phase feeds too.
fix: The q-line is the locus of (x, y) pairs of passing streams that satisfy the balance around the feed stage. At the point where the streams have the feed composition itself, x = y = x_F, so every q-line, whatever the feed condition, passes through (x_F, x_F).

problem: The stripping line is plotted up to x ≈ 0.66, well past P at x = 0.40. Above the feed the operating line in use is the rectifying line, so the extra segment can make a reader think the stripping line applies there.
fix: End the stripping-line series at P (0.40, 0.5833), or draw it only for x ≤ 0.40.
